title: Class-Name String Matching for Dynamic Dispatch
pattern: Evaluating type-name strings inside centralized control modules to determine behavior, recreating dynamic dispatch.
why_bad: It violates basic encapsulation and increases coupling. Adding a new class requires finding and modifying string matchers inside distant dispatch systems.
detection: The use of `target_class` strings or `any::type_name` queries inside conditionals to execute class-specific behavior.
counterexample: `None`. Standard polymorphic dispatch is always superior.
source: Sandi Metz - _Practical Object-oriented Design. An agile Primer ising Ruby [2nd ed.]_ (2019, Addison-Wesley).pdf, Chapter 7 "Schedule expects targets to know their own lead time".
